answer: At a garden observatory, agents selling comet measurements must reserve a separate 100-unit bond for each 10-unit payment. After submissions close, a public random beacon selects 20 percent of jobs for independent checks against reference observations. Proven fabrication forfeits the bond, while payments wait through the audit window. A fabricated job risks an expected 20-unit loss for at most 10 units gained; splitting jobs among aliases does not change the sampling rate or reuse bonds. Unbiased randomness, reliable reference data and an appeal process are essential.
